subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme.com>, priyom_das@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Hi Lina — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

What we heard (pain & goals):
- Primary pain: inconsistent response latency from current LLM infra causing poor UX during peak traffic (~200 rps bursts).
- Goals: 99th percentile latency under 300ms for text-gen flows; reduce per-token cost by ~30% with caching/quantization; support structured output for downstream ingestion.

Product fit / integration notes we discussed:
- SDK + API: Redwood’s JS/ Python SDKs can be dropped in for request routing; we’ll provide example snippets for streaming responses and function-calling.
- Function calling: can be used to reliably extract structured order confirmation objects (we sketched the schema on the call).
- Streaming: built-in streaming with partial tokens to speed perceived latency in client apps.
- Embeddings & reranking: we suggested using embeddings for semantic search + a lightweight reranker to reduce token usage and improve precision for product-recommendation flows.
- Ops: prefix/KV caching and adaptive batching to control cost during bursts.

Immediate next steps (action owners & dates):
1) Red team: send integration proposal + sample SDK snippets (Marissa) — by Tue 2027-06-01.
2) Acme: share example payloads and the schema you want for structured outputs (Lina) — by Fri 2027-06-04.
3) Technical deep-dive: 45-min call with Vivek (solutions eng) to review SDK changes and function-calling paths — propose Wed 2027-06-02 or Thu 2027-06-03.
4) Security docs: we attached SOC2 + short ops notes; procurement will need these for review.

Attachments: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf (proposal + pricing bands), SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf, proposed-aws-arch.png

If that looks right I’ll send a calendar invite for the deep-dive with Vivek and Priyom.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
https://redwood.ai

From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 17:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this summary is great and matches what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications: 

- The 99th percentile latency target is for our checkout and recommendations endpoints only (not analytics batch jobs).
- For structured outputs we’ll need the schema to include: order_id, items[{sku,qty,price}], total_amount, currency, and a confidence score.

Next items from our side:
- I’ll loop in our engineering lead (cc’ed procurement for timeline/contract). We can provide example payloads by end of week.
- Procurement asked if you can share an estimated pricing band for monthly committed tokens and a short SCT (service contract template) so our legal team can triage.

Can Vivek do the technical deep-dive on Wed 6/2 at 10am PT? If so we’ll accept.

Best,
Lina
Lina Gomez
Head of Product, Acme Corp
lina.gomez@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Perfect — thanks Lina. Wed 6/2 at 10am PT works for Vivek. I’ve attached the proposal and SOC2 cert for procurement. 

Attached: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf (contains example monthly pricing bands for committed capacity and overage), SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf

Quick notes on the SDK & implementation surface so engineering has context before the deep-dive:
- SDK changes: we’ll provide a sample streaming client in both JS and Python that shows chunked responses + a small retry/backoff helper.
- Function calling: recommended pattern is to register a lightweight schema at call-time and use the function-calling result to populate your order object; we’ll demo the exact mapping in the deep-dive.
- Structured outputs: we can return JSON-LD style objects or a compact JSON blob; you can choose based on downstream parsing needs.
- Embeddings + reranker: propose a two-step flow — index embeddings for search, then run a low-cost reranker model for top-K to improve precision; this reduces downstream token costs.

I’ll send the calendar invite for Wed 2027-06-02 10:00 PT with a short agenda (SDK walkthrough, function-calling example, ops & security Qs).

Regards,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Vivek / Priyom — forwarding Lina’s confirmation. Quick internal checklist before the deep-dive: 

- Vivek: have a short demo ready that shows streaming vs non-streaming UX differences and the function-calling mapping to their order schema. Bring the JS snippet for streaming.
- Priyom: draft a 1-pager on quantization/embedding costs and a recommended reranker (model size + expected token reduction).
- Ops: be ready to explain prefix caching and expected cost change for bursts; we should show a couple of numbers based on their estimated 200 rps peaks.

Keep it tight — 45 minutes. I’ll handle the calendar and procurement follow-up.

-M
